title: What if you made toast on Venus?
caption:
Venus is hotter than your oven. 🍞🪐

Venus' surface averages about 464 °C (NASA), nearly twice a home oven's top setting (≈260–290 °C).

The air there presses about 90 times harder than on Earth (92 bar), and it is 96.5% carbon dioxide.

Hold out a slice of bread and it never turns golden: plant matter starts breaking down above ~280 °C, and 400–500 °C is charcoal-making heat.

It would never catch fire either. There is no free oxygen, so nothing can burn. It just chars.

Send this to the friend who burns every toast.

Tomorrow: your weight on Jupiter.

⚠️ Don't try this. Overheated toasters and ovens can start real kitchen fires.
